biomarkers.name: CD5, CD117 (KIT)
biomarkers.prevalence: CD5+ and/or CD117+ in a substantial subset; co-expression is characteristic but not universal
biomarkers.clinical_use: Supports distinction of thymic carcinoma from thymoma and from some non-thymic carcinomas in the appropriate morphologic context

biomarkers.name: KIT mutations
biomarkers.clinical_use: Rare actionable subset; KIT-mutant thymic carcinoma may respond to KIT-directed therapy in selected cases

biomarkers.name: TP53
biomarkers.clinical_use: Common recurrent alteration; generally associated with aggressive biology rather than a validated routine clinical biomarker

biomarkers.name: PD-L1
biomarkers.prevalence: Often expressed, with high expression reported in a substantial subset
biomarkers.clinical_use: May help support use of immune checkpoint inhibition in recurrent/metastatic disease, although predictive value is imperfect and immune-related toxicity remains important

biomarkers.name: CYLD alteration
biomarkers.prevalence: Enriched in a subset of thymic squamous cell carcinomas, especially those with adenoid cystic carcinoma-like features
biomarkers.clinical_use: Supports recognition of a distinctive thymic carcinoma subset

biomarkers.name: CDKN2A/CDKN2B loss
biomarkers.clinical_use: Common genomic event in thymic carcinoma; not a standard standalone clinical biomarker

histomorphological_subtype.primary_pattern: Overtly malignant epithelial cells without the immature T-cell infiltrate characteristic of thymoma

tumor_microenvironment.immune_context: More conventional 'inflamed' pattern than thymoma; PD-L1 often expressed

cellular_states_and_lineage.cell_of_origin: Thymic epithelial cells with malignant transformation and loss of organotypic differentiation
cellular_states_and_lineage.differentiation_state: Undifferentiated or squamous — loses organotypic thymic differentiation that characterises thymoma
cellular_states_and_lineage.lineage_plasticity: Loss of organotypic thymic function distinguishes from thymoma (which retains T-cell selection function  autoimmune paraneoplastic syndromes)
